MPX2482 is a clinical report of a 2 y.o.  female  patient suffering from a Canavan Disease  displayed in MR - T2 weighted . 2 y.o. girl whose parents noted irritability in early neonatal course.  This improved by 5 months of age when patient was noted to be hypotonic.

She was also diagnosed in infancy with cortical blindness and has developmentally delay.  Head size noted to be large. The disease Canavan Disease  located in Brain and Neuro (Head). About Canavan Disease  we can say that: -AR (autosomal recessive)
-Most common in Ashkenazi Jews
-Deficiency in aspartoacylase
-Macrocephaly, seizures
-Death usually occurs in 2nd year of life

Imaging Findings:
-Diffuse, symmetric involvement of cerebral white matter
-SC WM preferentially affected early
-No contrast enhancement
-MRS: Elevation of NAA
Both the NAA to choline (Cho) and NAA to creatine (Cr) ratios are increased, with relatively normal Cho and Cr.

MPX1581 is a clinical report of a 29 y.o.  female  patient suffering from a Colloid cyst.  displayed in MR - T1W - noncontrast . 29 year old female with worsening headaches. The disease Colloid cyst.  located in Brain and Neuro (Head) and it can be treated in this way:  can be treated in this way: No treatment. Being followed by neurosurgery with serial examinations.. About Colloid (neuroepithelial) cyst of the third ventricle  we can say that: Colloid  cysts  are  uncommon  benign cysts of the anterior superior third ventricle, which are thought to arise  from  embryologic tissues  of  the  paraphysis, ependyma, or choroid plexus.  These lesions typically present in young adults in the  2nd to 5th   decade   with   complaints  referable  to  acute  or  chronic hydrocephalus.  Other symptoms include ataxia, memory disturbances, and gait disorders.    The  cyst  contents  include  secretory  and breakdown  products  of the epithelial lining tissue, including hemorrhage, lipid (cholesterol), hemosiderin, and CSF.  

On  T1-weighted MR images, these cysts vary widely from hypo- to hyperintense in comparison to normal brain.  Although they may be bright on T2-weighted images, moderate  to  marked hypointensity  is  common and has been attributed to a very  short  T1  relaxation  time  or  to  magnetic susceptibility effect from paramagnetic substances in the cyst.  On noncontrast  MR,  these lesions occasionally are indistinguishable by intensity from neoplasia; however, the absence  of  enhancement, classic location,  and  relative hypointensity  on  T2-weighted studies should suggest this diagnosis.  Treatment is variable, including  ventricular  shunting alone, stereotactic cyst drainage, or surgical resection.

On  noncontrast CT, colloid cysts are solitary, round to oval, usually hyperdense masses at the foramen of Monro  with  associated enlargement  of  one or both lateral ventricles (Film .3).  Minimal or absent contrast enhancement is typical.  Moderate  enhancement with  contrast  suggests  a  different  etiology,  such  as glioma, craniopharyngioma, choroid plexus papilloma,  or  remotely  meningioma.    Other  cystic  masses  such as arachnoid or ependymal cysts will mimic CSF in density and intensity. .
